summary: The Currency converter takes the numbers you enter and reports to currency (Convert to a popular currency) immediately. It is free to use, needs no account, and shows the working rather than just the answer. It suits a budget, a loan conversation, a payslip check or a what-if before you talk to a lender. Nothing is submitted anywhere: the arithmetic runs in the page you are looking at.

sections.title: How does the Currency converter calculator work?
sections.html:
The Currency converter takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports to currency (Convert to a popular currency) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in from currency.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Currency converter calculator
sections.html:
This is a conversion rather than a calculation. To currency (Convert to a popular currency) and from currency describe the same quantity, so the arithmetic underneath is a simple identity: whatever you type in one box is converted to a common base unit, and the other box is rendered from that base in its own unit.

That is why changing the unit chip does not change the underlying value, only the way it is written — and why you can enter a figure in either box and read the answer from the other.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• Shown in US Dollar, and convertible to any of the 113 units on that chip.
  • Shown in Denmark Krone, and convertible to any of the 113 units on that chip.

Before doubting the arithmetic, check the inputs: a unit chip on the wrong setting, a drop-down left at its default, or a percentage typed as a whole number rather than a decimal will each shift the answer by a clean power of ten.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

  • Currency, opening in US Dollar
  • Currency, opening in US Dollar
  • Currency, opening in Denmark Krone

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Currency converter earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Building a monthly budget and testing how one number shifts the rest
  • Comparing two offers that quote their costs in different ways
  • Sizing up a purchase before you commit to it
  • Any time the same 1 figures keep coming back — from currency — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

sections.title: What are the limits worth knowing?
sections.html:
Every tool draws a boundary somewhere. For the Currency converter, these are the ones that matter:

  • The unit chips cover the units listed on the page. A historical or regional unit that is missing can still be used by converting it to a listed unit first.
  • The calculator reports what the relationship implies; it does not judge whether the inputs themselves are sensible, so a figure that is out by a factor of ten will produce an answer that is out by the same factor.

sections.title: How do you check the answer yourself?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time — from currency for instance — and watch which results move. A result that stays put does not depend on it.
  • Try a round value you can work out in your head. If the answer matches your mental arithmetic, the inputs are on the scale you assumed.
  • Switch the units to the ones you normally use and confirm the numbers are unchanged apart from their label; if they are not, a chip was on the wrong setting.

faq.q: What does the Currency converter calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns to currency (Convert to a popular currency), derived from from currency. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Currency converter calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for from currency, which is a single field. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter from currency in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. From currency opens in US Dollar and the chip beside it offers 113 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: Is the Currency converter calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
